text:
incident-bot: Pager: kv-cache-p99 spike in inference-prod (us-west-2). alert_id=INC-9984. Autoscaling attempted, saw failed allocations. --link https://ops.redwood/incidents/INC-9984 :rotating_light:

Alex R: I'm primary for this window, picking up. Priya you're sec, can you confirm any ongoing customer-facing errors?

Priya N: seeing 15% 5xx on hosted-api route /v1/generate in us-west-2. Affected customers: a few PLG apps, small spike in error budget alerts. Not widespread yet.

Sara L: adding runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash (short checklist at top). Quick note: check prefix cache and redis connection pool first.

Tim G: quick triage: run `redis-cli -h kv-prod-01.cluster -c INFO` and check `used_memory_rss` + `connected_clients`. I saw stale client connections earlier.

Alex R: ok doing redis check now. if client count > 2000, we'll do a rolling restart of the cache pods. Will call it before restart.

Alex R: (after 60s) redis looks fine, connected_clients ~420, mem normal. Trace shows slowdown from model-serving nodes waiting on KV fetches. probably kvcache client stalls.

Priya N: can we warmstart a spare pool? There's a coverage gap 20:00-21:00 UTC in us-west-2 for Dedicated; burst capacity is limited. Suggest route-to-fallback policy to stop hard latency SLO breaches.

Alex R: agreed. I'm flipping a canary route to the smaller-latency model for risky customers. Command I used: `ryu route set --policy fallback --target small-llama-v1 --selector "team:plg" --region us-west-2` (internal tool).

Sara L: documented note: short fixes list (copy into incident):
- route risky customers to small-llama-v1 fallback
- restart model-client on affected nodes: `kubectl -n inference-prod rollout restart deploy/model-client --selector=zone=us-west-2`
- trigger warmstart of dedicated-pool-burst: https://console.redwood/dedicated/pools/burst/us-west-2
- escalate to infra if allocation fails after 2 attempts

Tim G: quick restart performed on two model-client pods. logs attached (truncated):
```
I0315 17:34:22 model-client starting
I0315 17:34:23 connected to kv-cache v1
I0315 17:34:24 serving traffic
```

Alex R: latency dropped from 620ms p99 -> 190ms p99 for the test slice after the restart and route flip. Good sign.

OpsEscalation: flagging for postmortem: need to verify why client stalls happen on scale-up. Will open ticket PM-453 (assigned to infra).

Priya N: on shift handoff: I'm taking over primary at 20:30 UTC. Action items for handoff note: add link to this thread, attach incidentbot timeline, confirm dedicated burst capacity steady, confirm no ongoing 5xx > 5% for 15m window.

Alex R: leaving a quick checklist to paste into the handoff message:
```
- Incident status: mitigated/monitoring
- Actions taken: route fallback + model-client restarts
- Next steps: infra ticket PM-453, follow-up: add health checks for kvcache client stalls
- Handoff ETA: 20:30 UTC to Priya N
- Runbooks referenced: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash
```

Sara L: I pinned the runbook + the console warmstart page to the channel. Also added a short one-liner runbook summary to the ticket so oncall can act faster next time. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Handoff logged: primary change scheduled 20:30 UTC -> Priya N. Update: incident status set to MONITORING.

Alex R: leaving. Priya — ping me if it regresses, otherwise I'll join postmortem. :wave:

Priya N: got it, taking over. I'll validate 15m window then mark resolved if stable. Adding follow-up item: add automatic fallback when kvcache latency > 300ms for 2m.

Tim G: quick note for the PM: consider increasing client connection pool timeouts and add circuit-breaker in model-client to avoid backpressure from stalled kvcache calls.

OpsEscalation: opened PM-453 and assigned to infra team lead. Logging this thread to the incident timeline.

Sara L: thanks team. Short-term remedies worked. We'll flesh out the long-term fix in PM-453 and schedule a ops runbook tidy-up session. :coffee:
